test_recommendation.text:
A conforming implementation SHOULD include tests that cover the behaviors defined in this
specification.

core_required.text: - `Core Conformance`: deterministic tests REQUIRED for all conforming implementations.

extension_required.text:
- `Extension Conformance`: REQUIRED only for OPTIONAL features that an implementation chooses to
  ship.

real_integration_recommended.text:
- `Real Integration Profile`: environment-dependent smoke/integration checks RECOMMENDED before
  production use.

section17_profile.text:
Unless otherwise noted, Sections 17.1 through 17.7 are `Core Conformance`. Bullets that begin with
`If ... is implemented` are `Extension Conformance`.

section18_profile.text:
Use the same validation profiles as Section 17:

- Section 18.1 = `Core Conformance`
- Section 18.2 = `Extension Conformance`
- Section 18.3 = `Real Integration Profile`

real_integration_skipping.text:
These checks are RECOMMENDED for production readiness and MAY be skipped in CI when credentials,
network access, or external service permissions are unavailable.

rules: Every approved requirement ID appears exactly once in each candidate/profile report.
Case deletion, renaming, overlap, or related_requirement_ids cannot remove a requirement obligation.
Unimplemented cases produce incomplete with reason unimplemented, never pass.
Only pass satisfies an applicable requirement; harness health and cleanup must also be complete.
Core unsupported, unobservable, incomplete, skipped, or harness_error cannot earn complete core conformance.
Conditional feature presence makes its checks required; unknown presence is incomplete.
Conditional not_applicable requires a checked absence declaration; missing traffic is not absence.
Real-integration skipping is explicit and requires no fabricated passing claim.
Profiles translate operations and documented raw observations, never verdicts or normative expectations.

terminology_resolution.research_Unsupported: not_applicable only for checked conditional absence; otherwise incomplete with reason unsupported.
terminology_resolution.Unimplemented: Case implementation state and incomplete reason, not a passing run verdict.
terminology_resolution.unobservable: An observation boundary, not evidence of correct candidate behavior.

report_contract.harness_health: Separate setup, capture, fixture, process ownership, cleanup, and report integrity results invalidate earlier passes on failure.

observation_vocabulary.partial: Behavior is partially external; an exact category, value, or internal fact needs a declared observation.
observation_vocabulary.unobservable: Mandatory service contract alone exposes neither the fact nor the necessary invocation.

families.WF: CONFORMANCE.md §18.1 table: workflow_document/config_value + workflow_parser examples/models passed locally; explicit/default CLI cases pass.
families.CFG: Same table: config_test defaults/env/path/numeric/state cases passed locally; strict template tests passed under the documented Jinja profile.
families.RELOAD: Same table and Live executable assembly: last-good reload/epoch/preflight model cases and invalid reload executable regressions pass.
families.WS: Same table: key/hash/owner models and native directory/store descriptor/lock/replacement/rollback cases passed locally and hosted.
families.HOOK: Same table: four hooks, configurable timeouts, fake and native hook/lifecycle cases passed locally and hosted.
families.TRACK: Same table plus docs/adapters/linear.md: ordered states/atomic ID reads, normalization/binding/paging models, native HTTPS and tracker CLI gates documented passed. The profile publishes bounds/routing/errors.
families.CORE: Same table and Additional requested gates: pure list/event model, exact command comparisons, service simulation and executable dispatch/preflight cases documented passed.
families.RETRY: Same table: pure backoff/cap and Eio mock timers passed; native-service retry-cap and startup-cleanup cells explicitly remain pending.
families.PROTO: Same table and closed-runner paragraphs: schema codec67/42, native byte-framing/three-turn/usage/timeout/interruption/drain cases documented passed. This is fake-peer evidence, not real Codex/auth/sandbox acceptance.
families.LOG: Required-log table and Live executable assembly: canonical issue_identifier/session closure, escaped records, early reporting and native output failure regressions documented passed.
families.STATUS: Status API checkpoint: local immutable projection, route/query/availability and normal/optimized status CLI gates documented passed; PR13 hosted review is still pending.
families.CLI: Workflow/CLI table and Live executable assembly: positional/default/startup/signal/exit behavior documented passed locally and through PR12 hosted gates.
families.—: No row-specific passing evidence established by these text reads; a plan or a broad suite count is not a passing case.

evidence_boundaries: No approved requirement has an implemented portable case or portable pass in this catalog.
Existing local/model/native/hosted results are documentation context, not newly verified or portable evidence.
Optional HTTP, clock control, adapter probes, and test surfaces are declared capabilities rather than new baseline production requirements.
Single-authority and internal type representations require separately audited design/model evidence; finite black-box behavior does not prove them.
Workspace containment tests have finite host/race bounds; black-box samples do not prove safety under arbitrary host races.
PID markers and ESRCH probes are point-in-time observations, not historical reap attestation.
Acknowledged requests or signals are not completed reconciliation, child closure, or owned-process join.
Candidate-authored logs or saved manifest flags cannot substitute for missing raw observations.
Fixture fake-peer evidence does not establish real Codex auth, sandbox enforcement, real-provider acceptance, or clean-host release qualification.
Real provider/Codex trials are opt-in and remain unauthorized for this checkpoint.

source.text:
- A real tracker smoke test can be run with valid credentials supplied through the selected
  adapter's documented secret mechanism.

- Real integration tests SHOULD use isolated test identifiers/workspaces and clean up tracker
  artifacts when practical.
- A skipped real-integration test SHOULD be reported as skipped, not silently treated as passed.

- If a real-integration profile is explicitly enabled in CI or release validation, failures SHOULD
  fail that job.

- HTTP server extension honors CLI `--port` over `server.port`, uses a safe default bind host, and
  exposes the baseline endpoints/error semantics in Section 13.7 if shipped.

- Provider-native agent tools, when shipped, execute through the app-server session using
  host-side configured adapter auth without passing tracker secrets to the child.
- TODO: Persist retry queue and session metadata across process restarts.

- TODO: Make observability settings configurable in workflow front matter without prescribing UI
  implementation details.

- TODO: Extract common semantic helper tools only after multiple adapters demonstrate real
  duplication; do not preemptively replace provider-native tools with generic CRUD.
- Run the `Real Integration Profile` from Section 17.8 with valid credentials and network access.
- Verify hook execution and workflow path resolution on the target host OS/shell environment.

- If the OPTIONAL HTTP server is shipped, verify the configured port behavior and loopback/default
  bind expectations on the target environment.
